prompt: Write 10 distinct notes the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual made about one member each while helping them with: a member in hospital during a claim. Each says what will help the next time this agent serves this member: how they like to be dealt with, what is still open, what to check. One or two sentences, third person, no names. This batch leans towards retired members and older homeowners. Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"Member was in hospital when contacted, so future calls should go to the nominated relative first and be kept brief, calm and practical."},{"type":"preference","content":"Prefers straightforward updates in plain English and appreciates one clear next step at a time rather than a long list of actions."},{"type":"fact","content":"Claim remains open pending confirmation of hospital discharge, after which the member can confirm access to the property and provide any missing details."},{"type":"observation","content":"Older homeowner, likely to need extra time to gather papers, so allow for slower responses and offer to repeat any key points."},{"type":"fact","content":"Need to check whether emergency repairs were arranged during the hospital stay and whether any invoices or photos have been sent in yet."},{"type":"preference","content":"Likes reassurance that nothing urgent will be missed and responds well when the agent summarises what has already been done before asking for anything else."},{"type":"observation","content":"Member was distressed about dealing with the claim from hospital, so future contact should avoid jargon and keep the tone steady and patient."},{"type":"fact","content":"Still open to confirm who can authorise property access, whether a neighbour or family member can assist, and whether the loss has changed since first report."},{"type":"preference","content":"Prefers morning contact when possible and is less comfortable with digital-only updates, so a phone call is better than email alone."},{"type":"observation","content":"Member may need help recalling dates and details after the hospital admission, so check the timeline carefully and be ready to note information from a carer or relative."}]}
